title: Navier × Grab
subtitle: SEA water-mobility — ridehail integrated across 19 cities
executive_summary: Grab is Navier's single highest-leverage growth opportunity in SEA. The super-app already owns last-mile demand across 19 markets where surface water-mobility is undersupplied, congested, or simply missing. Navier brings the asset — hydrofoiling electric and hybrid vessels with a 700 nm range envelope on Quanta-LR — and the network operating model. A regional partnership across SEA converts Grab's existing demand into water-mode revenue and positions Navier across the fastest-emerging archipelagic mobility region globally.

narrative.headline: Singapore — SEA Quanta-LR Hub
narrative.body: Pilot anchor. Singapore is the regional Quanta-LR hub: MPA-friendly waters, certification-credible flag, 11 berthing/charging POIs already mapped (Marina Bay → Sentosa → Jurong → Tuas). Phase 1 launches Pioneer II inter-island commutes (Marina Bay ↔ Sentosa, ~3 nm; Marina Bay ↔ Lazarus, ~5 nm) inside the GrabRide product. Phase 2 stands up the Singapore-radial Quanta-LR fan to Batam, Bintan, Tioman, Desaru — all sub-300 nm, all already routed in our spine.

narrative.headline: Bali — Pioneer II tourist commute + Nusa entry point
narrative.body: Pilot 2. Benoa ↔ Nusa Penida/Lembongan is the dominant water-taxi corridor today; current fleet is slow, wet, weather-exposed. Pioneer II runs the route at 30 kts in foil, dry cabin, 12 pax. Grab integration adds a hotel-pickup → boat-transfer → island-resort booking in a single super-app flow. Hospitality cluster (Bvlgari, Aman, COMO, Six Senses) is the upsell layer for higher-yield charter inventory.

narrative.headline: Bangkok — Chao Phraya commute + Pattaya entry point
narrative.body: Pilot 3. Chao Phraya river-line congestion is one of SEA's worst urban commute problems. Pioneer II foils above the chop quietly with no wake — a regulator-friendly story. Quanta-LR extends to Pattaya (~85 nm, Pioneer II edge / Quanta-LR comfortable) and Koh Samet. Competitor presence (Candela) = market-validation; Navier wins on Quanta-LR range and software.

narrative.headline: Phuket / Phang Nga — Andaman cluster
narrative.body: Steady-state. Phuket marina hubs anchor a Quanta-LR fan into Phang Nga Bay, Phi Phi, Krabi, and onward to Langkawi (cross-border, ~70 nm). Hospitality cluster: Aman, Soneva, Banyan Tree. Grab is already deeply embedded in Phuket inbound tourism flow — boat-mode integrates into existing airport→resort flows.

narrative.headline: Koh Samui / Phangan / Tao — Gulf triangle
narrative.body: Steady-state. Inter-island hop triangle: all sub-30 nm legs, Pioneer II ideal. Replaces existing ferry pain (long, slow, weather-dependent). Hospitality: Six Senses, Anantara, Banyan Tree all on-island.

narrative.headline: Langkawi — Andaman cross-border
narrative.body: Steady-state. Langkawi ↔ Phuket cross-border Quanta-LR entry point unlocks a previously-impossible direct route (currently ferry + bus + flight). Cross-border ridehail + immigration coordination via Grab's existing MY/TH operating relationships.

narrative.headline: Philippines — archipelagic Quanta-LR play
narrative.body: Steady-state. PH is the largest unsolved archipelagic mobility market in SEA. Manila → Boracay, Cebu → Bohol, Palawan inter-island. Grab Philippines is the #1 super-app — boat-mode is a structural addition to their inventory.

narrative.headline: Jakarta — Pulau Seribu + IKN adjacency
narrative.body: Steady-state. Pulau Seribu (Thousand Islands) Pioneer II fan from Ancol. Strategic: Jakarta is the ID base for the IKN Nusantara new-capital relocation — first global instance of new-capital greenfield mobility adjacency.

narrative.headline: Riau Islands — Singapore cross-border
narrative.body: Steady-state. Batam, Bintan, Karimun all sub-50 nm from Singapore — Pioneer II routes today. Anambas/Natuna are Quanta-LR entry points (sister-quad architecture). Cross-border ridehail SGP↔ID is the Grab Singapore + Grab Indonesia integration moment.

narrative.headline: Lombok — Mandalika DPSP
narrative.body: Steady-state. Mandalika is one of Indonesia's 5 priority super-priority destinations (DPSP). Quanta-LR refuel-mid-node at Lembar. Connects Bali ↔ Lombok ↔ Gili Islands ↔ Komodo on a single network.

narrative.headline: Komodo / Flores — Labuan Bajo DPSP
narrative.body: Steady-state. Second of the 5 DPSP destinations. Labuan Bajo is the gateway; Komodo NP boats today are slow and crowded. Pioneer II for in-park hops; Quanta-LR for Bali↔Labuan Bajo (~250 nm) which currently requires a flight.

narrative.headline: Raja Ampat — premium liveaboard entry point
narrative.body: Steady-state. Top-tier dive destination; current access is multi-hour open-skiff transfer. Quanta-LR entry point premium-positioned with Aqua Expeditions and the resort cluster.

narrative.headline: Wakatobi — Quanta-LR refuel-mid-node
narrative.body: Steady-state. Wakatobi resort + diving cluster; refuel-mid-node in our spine. Quanta-LR connects to Komodo and onward.

narrative.headline: Derawan / Berau — Kalimantan dive cluster
narrative.body: Steady-state. Refuel-mid-node. Sangalaki/Kakaban manta + jellyfish lake premium entry point.

narrative.headline: Banda / Maluku — spice-route heritage cluster
narrative.body: Steady-state. Quanta-LR-only market — historic spice route geography; Banda Neira heritage tourism, no current fast-ferry option.

narrative.headline: Lake Toba — inland DPSP
narrative.body: Steady-state. Inland-lake market (only inland market in the Grab/Navier overlap). DPSP destination. Pioneer II all-electric is uniquely suited to a clean inland lake.

narrative.headline: Vietnam — Halong, Da Nang, Phu Quoc
narrative.body: Steady-state. Halong Bay tourism entry point; Da Nang ↔ Hoi An coastal commute; Phu Quoc island-hopping. Grab Vietnam is dominant.

narrative.headline: Malaysia — Penang + Tioman + east coast
narrative.body: Steady-state. Penang island commute, Tioman ↔ Mersing (~55 nm corrected), east-coast hospitality. Grab MY base.

narrative.headline: Cambodia — Sihanoukville + Koh Rong + Taj
narrative.body: Steady-state. Sihanoukville ↔ Koh Rong / Koh Rong Samloem Pioneer II. Cambodia is a natural luxury-hospitality entry point anchored by a leading global hotel group.

title: Navier × Careem
subtitle: MENA water-mobility — super-app integrated across the GCC
executive_summary: Careem is the MENA mirror of the Grab opportunity in SEA — an established regional super-app covering 10 cities across the GCC and Red Sea where Navier has filled or stub city files. The opportunity: convert existing super-app demand into water-mode revenue across intra-city (Pioneer II) and intra-GCC cross-border (Quanta-LR) corridors. A Careem partnership is regulator-light versus public-transit deals — making it the fastest MENA path to landed revenue and a parallel de-risk for the government-channel work. Careem is now part of Uber, so a Careem regional partnership simultaneously opens a global Uber conversation.

narrative.headline: Dubai — anchor city, first boat in 2 weeks
narrative.body: Anchor and time-sensitive. First boat arrives in ~2 weeks; Careem is the fastest path to revenue while RTA is . CareemRide water-mode launches on Marina ↔ Bluewaters ↔ Palm ↔ Mina Rashid as a premium product. 14 berthing POIs already mapped at real OSM coords.

narrative.headline: Doha — Lusail + Katara + The Pearl
narrative.body: Pilot 2. Doha intra-city: Lusail Marina ↔ The Pearl ↔ Katara ↔ Banana Island. All <30 nm — Pioneer II. Katara is the Qatar hospitality/culture cluster. Cross-border Quanta-LR: Dubai ↔ Doha (~200 nm) as a same-day GCC business connector — currently a flight + transit.

narrative.headline: Manama — Amwaj + Reef Island + Dammam cross-border
narrative.body: Pilot 3. Manama intra-city + Bahrain ↔ Eastern Province KSA (Dammam, ~30 nm) cross-border — Pioneer II edge / Quanta-LR comfortable. Replaces the King Fahd Causeway congestion for premium time-sensitive travel.

narrative.headline: Abu Dhabi — Saadiyat + Yas + Western Region
narrative.body: Steady-state. Careem AD operations integrate with Saadiyat cultural cluster, Yas leisure, and Western Region Anantara entry point (Sir Bani Yas Quanta-LR).

narrative.headline: Sharjah — Khor Fakkan east-coast crossover
narrative.body: Steady-state. Sharjah's east-coast enclave (Khor Fakkan) on the Gulf of Oman is a Quanta-LR refuel-mid-node for the Musandam (Khasab) cross-border entry point.

narrative.headline: Ras Al Khaimah — Hayat/Marjan + Musandam cross-border
narrative.body: Steady-state. RAK ↔ Khasab (Oman exclave, ~25 nm cross-border) is a Pioneer II entry point — currently a 90-min drive across a border. UAE-flag precedent on this corridor is an open confirm item.

narrative.headline: Fujairah — east-coast Gulf of Oman
narrative.body: Steady-state. Fujairah ↔ Khor Fakkan ↔ Dibba intra-city Pioneer II + onward to Musandam Quanta-LR.

narrative.headline: Muscat — Bandar Jissah + Six Senses Zighy Bay
narrative.body: Steady-state. Muscat ↔ Bandar Jissah ↔ Daymaniyat Islands Pioneer II. Six Senses Zighy Bay (Musandam) is a premium hospitality anchor reachable via Quanta-LR from Dubai/RAK.

narrative.headline: Jeddah — Red Sea gateway + RSG adjacency
narrative.body: Steady-state. Jeddah is the operational gateway for Red Sea Global; Careem KSA is the demand layer for both Jeddah waterfront and RSG transfer logistics.

narrative.headline: Sharm El Sheikh — Red Sea South + RSG cross-border adjacency
narrative.body: Steady-state. Sinai resort cluster; near Red Sea Global on opposite shore. Cross-border Quanta-LR entry point into Saudi Red Sea coast as RSG matures.

title: Navier × UAE Waterfront
subtitle: Quiet electric foiling across Dubai & Abu Dhabi — transit, hospitality, cross-emirate
partner_org_canonical_name: UAE Transport Authorities (Dubai RTA + Abu Dhabi ITC)

headline_metrics.label: Emirates in scope
headline_metrics.sub: two markets, one Quanta-LR hop apart

headline_metrics.label: Hospitality entry point
headline_metrics.sub: Palm, Saadiyat, Yas, Sir Bani Yas

headline_metrics.label: Local-build path
headline_metrics.sub: regional production hub candidate at scale

executive_summary: The UAE is Navier's first and most time-sensitive MENA market — the first vessel arrives within weeks. Two complementary openings sit one Quanta-LR hop apart. In Dubai, the Roads and Transport Authority (RTA) operates the existing abra and water-taxi network — the natural public-transit partner for a quiet, wakeless, all-electric Pioneer II upgrade plus a Marina ↔ Bluewaters ↔ Palm ↔ Mina Rashid premium connector. In Abu Dhabi, the Integrated Transport Centre (ITC) pairs with a deeper hospitality opening across Saadiyat, Yas, and the Sir Bani Yas island resorts, and stands as the strongest first regional production-hub candidate as the local market scales. Pioneer II covers every intra-city leg; Quanta-LR stitches the emirates together and reaches Sir Bani Yas, Khasab, Doha and Manama as long-range premium connectors. Engagement across both authorities is coordinated locally; private-operator outreach runs in parallel as the near-term revenue path.

narrative.headline: Dubai — abra corridor electrification + premium Marina connector
narrative.body: Anchor city. 14 berthing POIs already mapped at real OSM coords: Dubai Marina Mall, Bluewaters, Palm Jumeirah, Mina Rashid, Dubai Creek + the abra stations on both sides of the Creek + waterside hospitality (Atlantis, Burj Al Arab, Madinat Jumeirah). Pioneer II is uniquely fit: <70 nm, all-electric, quiet-mode in harbor, 30 kts foiling above chop. The RTA proposal is a 12-month pilot on one premium corridor (Marina ↔ Mina Rashid) plus one heritage corridor (Creek abra augmentation), with conversion option to full -pilot. Quanta-LR uplift unlocks Dubai ↔ Khasab (cross-border, UAE-flag precedent ), Dubai ↔ Sir Bani Yas, Dubai ↔ Doha as long-range premium connectors.

narrative.headline: Abu Dhabi — Saadiyat + Yas intra-city + Sir Bani Yas long-range
narrative.body: Anchor city. Intra-cluster: Saadiyat marina, Yas Marina, Eastern Mangroves, Zaya Nurai. All <30 nm legs — Pioneer II all-electric. Hospitality cluster: Anantara (Eastern Mangroves + Sir Bani Yas + Qasr Al Sarab), Four Seasons, Edition, Rosewood. The Sir Bani Yas Anantara jetty is in our manual coord overrides — strategic premium entry point. Quanta-LR unlocks Sir Bani Yas as a same-day round-trip from AD city (~150 nm one-way, ~3.5 hrs each way at 30 kts foiling — vs. current 2.5 hr drive + 30 min boat). Production-hub conversion: at ~50 boats AD shipyard becomes the regional MRO + light-build base.

title: Navier × Red Sea Global
subtitle: Greenfield hospitality cluster — Ocean Race 2027 as time-bound trigger

headline_metrics.label: Resort islands
headline_metrics.sub: Sheybarah, Ummahat, Coastal Village, multi-resort cluster

executive_summary: Red Sea Global is the single largest hospitality cluster opportunity in the global pipeline — a $50B+ greenfield development on the Saudi Red Sea coast with 16+ resort islands and zero existing surface-marine operator. The combination is unique: greenfield (no incumbent to displace), premium pricing power (ultra-luxury hospitality customer set), and a hard time-bound trigger in the Ocean Race Grand Finale 2027, which will put global attention on RSG waters and call for a visible, distinctive premium marine fleet. Quanta-LR commercial timing (H2 2026+) aligns with Ocean Race 2027 — the boats are ready, the showcase is built-in. Greenfield charging infrastructure means it can be specified from scratch; Quanta-LR removes the dependency entirely with refuel-anywhere range plus quiet electric operation in harbour.

narrative.headline: Red Sea Global — 16+ islands, greenfield premium fleet
narrative.body: Anchor cluster. Sheybarah, Ummahat, Coastal Village, and the broader 16+ island resort programme. All POIs are in our manual coord overrides (OSM doesn't index greenfield development). Pioneer II covers intra-cluster (all <70 nm). Quanta-LR (H2 2026+) unlocks RSG ↔ Jeddah (~250 nm) and RSG ↔ NEOM Sindalah (~180 nm) as same-day premium connectors. The model: an RSG-owned premium fleet scaled to the resort opening cadence, with the Ocean Race Grand Finale 2027 as the public showcase moment.

narrative.headline: Jeddah — operational gateway + Quanta-LR refuel-mid-node
narrative.body: Operational base. Jeddah is the air gateway for RSG inbound guests and a Quanta-LR refuel-mid-node on the Jeddah ↔ RSG (~250 nm) corridor. Jeddah waterfront also stands alone as a hospitality + Careem demand market.

narrative.headline: NEOM Sindalah — adjacent greenfield mega-cluster
narrative.body: Adjacent. NEOM Sindalah opens 2024–2025 with a yacht-club + 80+ berth marina and adjacent luxury resorts. RSG ↔ Sindalah (~180 nm) is a Quanta-LR corridor; the two clusters can be sold as a single integrated KSA Red Sea premium marine network.

title: Navier × Singapore MPA
subtitle: Maritime and Port Authority — certification-credible flag and SEA Quanta-LR hub
partner_org_canonical_name: Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore
executive_summary: Singapore Maritime and Port Authority (MPA) is the de-facto regulatory home base for SEA water-mobility and the most certification-credible flag in the region. The MPA story is a regulatory de-risk play that simultaneously unlocks (a) Singapore as the SEA Quanta-LR commercial hub, (b) the Singapore-radial cross-border Quanta-LR fan into Indonesia and Malaysia, and (c) certification credibility that accelerates every other SEA market including the Grab regional partnership. MPA is the lead agency; LTA supports intra-city commute integration. Singapore's progressive maritime regulator stance (electric harbour-craft mandates, autonomous-vessel sandboxing) makes it a willing first mover.

narrative.headline: Singapore — SEA Quanta-LR Hub
narrative.body: Anchor city. 11 berthing/charging POIs mapped: Marina Bay, Sentosa, Lazarus, Jurong, Tuas. MPA pilot scope: (1) Pioneer II inter-island commute (Marina Bay ↔ Sentosa, ~3 nm; Marina Bay ↔ Lazarus, ~5 nm) inside an electric-harbor-craft framework MPA already supports. (2) Singapore-radial Quanta-LR fan: Singapore ↔ Batam (~12 nm cross-border), Singapore ↔ Bintan (~25 nm), Singapore ↔ Tioman (~110 nm), Singapore ↔ Desaru (~25 nm). All routes in our spine. (3) Singapore-flagged registration as the certification anchor for Navier vessels operating across SEA — accelerates Grab regional rollout.

narrative.headline: Riau Islands — Singapore cross-border anchor
narrative.body: Steady-state. Batam, Bintan, Karimun: all sub-50 nm from Singapore — Pioneer II routes. Anambas/Natuna as Quanta-LR entry points. Singapore-flag + Indonesia bilateral water-mode framework is the MPA + IDN MoT joint workstream.

narrative.headline: Malaysia — cross-border to Desaru, Tioman, Mersing
narrative.body: Steady-state. Singapore ↔ Desaru, Singapore ↔ Tioman, Tioman ↔ Mersing (~55 nm corrected). MPA + Marine Department Malaysia bilateral on water-mode ridehail and tourism corridor regulation.

title: Navier × Qatar Waterborne Transit
subtitle: Doha Bay and Corniche — quiet electric harbour mobility
executive_summary: Doha's bay and Corniche are an ideal setting for quiet, fast, low-wake waterborne transit linking the cultural, commercial, and waterfront districts. Hydrofoil electric vessels offer a clean, high-throughput option that reduces road load and emissions while giving the waterfront a modern, low-noise mobility layer.

narrative.headline: Corniche + Old Doha Port
narrative.body: Named public boarding points at the Doha Corniche ferry station and the Old Doha Port cruise terminal anchor a harbour route network. Calm-bay conditions suit a near-zero-wake hydrofoil well.

partner_view.value_prop: A clean, quiet, high-throughput waterborne transit option for Doha Bay. Hydrofoil electric vessels link waterfront districts with zero direct emissions and minimal wake and noise — easing road congestion and adding a modern mobility layer to the Corniche.
partner_view.call_to_action: Trial an all-electric harbour route between the Corniche and Old Doha Port.

title: Abu Dhabi ITC × Navier — a premium, zero-emission layer for an island capital
subtitle: Abu Dhabi is a city of islands. Navier adds a fast, quiet, electric water layer above today's marine fleet — new high-value corridors and a credible path to decarbonize.
executive_summary: Navier adds a fast, quiet, electric water layer above your existing marine fleet — premium island corridors today's boats can't serve, additive to your current operators. Abu Dhabi 2040 and UAE Net Zero 2050 give top-cover for marine fleet renewal, and the emirate's geography — Yas, Saadiyat, Al Maryah, Lulu, Sir Bani Yas and the Corniche — is made for water mobility. Foiling makes those hops fast, smooth and silent, with no charging infrastructure required beyond a berth pedestal, and a hybrid long-range option for the Gulf corridor.

narrative.headline: Phase 1 — Island-core pilot
narrative.body: A five-vessel Pioneer II pilot connecting the Corniche, the CBD islands and the Saadiyat / Yas destinations — proving a quiet, zero-emission premium tier on sheltered inner waters, with clean first-of-class metrics for the authority.

narrative.headline: Phase 2 — Full island network
narrative.body: We light up the complete Abu Dhabi island network — a true marine layer of the city's transport system, with surge capacity for Yas events and reliable, weather-tolerant island shuttles that foiling makes comfortable year-round.

narrative.headline: Phase 3 — Gulf corridors: the long range
narrative.body: Quanta-LR's hybrid range turns the Gulf into part of the network: a smooth single-leg Abu Dhabi ↔ Dubai corridor and a direct line to the Western Region's Sir Bani Yas islands — routes that road can't match, with no charging-infrastructure dependency.

narrative.headline: Phase 4 — Southern Gulf network at scale
narrative.body: Steady state: 50+ foiling vessels run the full Abu Dhabi island mesh, the Western Region island chain on Quanta-LR, and a multi-daily express up to Dubai — the capital's integrated transport network extended onto the water, zero-emission end to end.

partner_view.value_prop: We work with the Integrated Transport Centre to introduce a software-defined foiling tier on top of Abu Dhabi's existing marine network. Pioneer II runs all-electric across the island core; Quanta-LR opens the long Gulf corridors that today require a road detour. It is additive — premium service and decarbonization — never a displacement of existing operators.
partner_view.call_to_action: An island-core pilot connecting the Corniche, Saadiyat and Yas.

title: Bolt × Navier — the European demand platform, now on the water
subtitle: Bolt owns the demand from the Aegean to the Gulf. The coastline is the surface it hasn't claimed yet.
executive_summary: Bolt already owns the demand in Europe's most water-bound markets. Navier supplies a uniform, software-defined, autonomy-ready foiling fleet that books door-to-door beside a Bolt car at every marina — turning slow ferries and pricey charters into an in-app water tier across the Mediterranean and the Gulf. Bolt's strongest seasonal demand peaks are in markets where roads run out and the water begins, on ferry fleets that are among Europe's oldest and most polluting — exactly as the EU and Gulf tighten marine emissions and a ~100-vessel Navier network ramps in the Maldives. The in-app water tier is open across the entire Bolt footprint, for now.

narrative.headline: Phase 1 — Mediterranean beachhead
narrative.body: Launch the in-app foiling tier in Bolt's deepest island markets — the Greek Saronic/Cyclades and the Dalmatian coast — proving the supply standard where ferry demand saturates.

narrative.headline: Phase 2 — the full Mediterranean
narrative.body: Extend across Italy (Amalfi + the zero-wake Venice lagoon) and the Côte d'Azur — a Mediterranean-wide Bolt water tier.

narrative.headline: Phase 3 — the Gulf
narrative.body: Carry the identical supply standard into Bolt's Gulf markets — the UAE coast and the Saudi Red Sea giga-projects — for a footprint spanning the Aegean to the Red Sea.

partner_view.value_prop: We add a Bolt-branded foiling water tier across Bolt's most water-bound markets — the Greek islands, the Dalmatian coast, the Italian Riviera and lagoon, the Côte d'Azur, and the Gulf. Navier supplies the software-defined fleet and the network playbook proven in the Maldives; Bolt brings the demand, the app and the dispatch. Start with one market or commit to the network — the supply standard is identical everywhere.
partner_view.call_to_action: Pick a beachhead market — Greece is the recommended entry — and sign a pilot MOU on three corridors.

title: Navier × Côte d'Azur — the Riviera, by foil
subtitle: Nice to Monaco in minutes, silent and over the water, while the Corniche sits in traffic.
executive_summary: The Riviera's destinations are all on the water, minutes apart by sea. A foiling-electric tier turns the coast into a silent, fast, zero-emission waterway — the helicopter experience at a fraction of the cost and noise, gliding past the traffic. The Riviera hosts the world's marquee events — the Cannes Film Festival, the Monaco Grand Prix, the Yacht Show — when road and helicopter capacity saturate completely. France and Monaco are both pushing hard on marine decarbonization and noise limits, and Monaco's Yacht Club and the region's marinas are actively courting electric propulsion. A foiling tier arrives exactly as the demand peaks and the diesel/helicopter alternatives come under pressure.

narrative.headline: Phase 1 — the Nice–Monaco spine
narrative.body: Launch the airport-to-Monaco corridor and the Nice–Cap Ferrat–Monaco coastal hop — the densest, most congested premium legs on the coast.

narrative.headline: Phase 2 — the full Riviera waterway
narrative.body: Extend west to Cannes, Antibes and Saint-Tropez, adding the Gulf of Saint-Tropez crossing and event-surge shuttle capacity for Cannes and the Grand Prix.

partner_view.value_prop: We bring a foiling-electric premium water tier to the French Riviera — linking Nice, Cannes, Antibes, Saint-Tropez and Monaco by sea. Navier supplies the software-defined fleet, captains and certification path; Riviera marina, hospitality and event partners bring the berths, the demand and the events calendar. Together we turn the most congested luxury coast in Europe into its fastest, quietest waterway.
partner_view.call_to_action: A pilot MOU on the Nice–Monaco corridor timed to a marquee event season.

title: Navier × D-Marin — marinas that move people
subtitle: Turning a pan-Mediterranean marina network into a foiling-electric mobility network.
executive_summary: D-Marin's marinas are the perfect berthing-and-charging backbone for a foiling-electric network. Navier turns a network of premium marinas into a network of premium mobility nodes — fast silent low-wake transfers between marinas, islands, resorts and airports, all charging at berths D-Marin already operates. D-Marin's marinas span exactly the Mediterranean clusters where Navier's island and coastal cases are sharpest — the Croatian islands, the Saronic and Cyclades, the Turkish coast, Montenegro's Boka Bay. Marinas already have the one thing electric mobility needs that destinations lack: shore power at every berth. The network and the charging are already built; the missing layer is the vessel.

narrative.headline: Phase 1 — Croatia island cluster
narrative.body: Launch from the D-Marin Croatian marinas (Mandalina/Šibenik, Borik) into the Split–Kornati–island corridors — the densest premium island-transfer demand against D-Marin's strongest berths.

narrative.headline: Phase 2 — Greece & Turkey clusters
narrative.body: Extend to the Greek (Zea, Gouvia) and Turkish (Didim, Turgutreis) marinas — Saronic, Cyclades and Bodrum-coast transfers between D-Marin berths and the islands.

narrative.headline: Phase 3 — pan-network mobility layer
narrative.body: A foiling-electric mobility layer across the D-Marin network — Croatia, Greece, Turkey, Montenegro and the UAE — marinas connected as charging-and-demand nodes.

partner_view.value_prop: Navier brings a software-defined foiling-electric fleet; D-Marin brings the berths, the charging backbone and the waterfront destinations across the Mediterranean. Together we connect the marinas D-Marin already owns into a clean, fast, branded mobility layer — marina-to-island, marina-to-airport and marina-to-marina — anchored on the live Maldives proof case.
partner_view.call_to_action: Launch the Croatian island cluster in 2027 and replicate marina-by-marina across the network.

title: Dubai RTA × Navier — a premium, zero-emission layer on the water
subtitle: A foiling tier that sits above today's marine network — new high-value corridors, a clear decarbonization path, and the abra trade left untouched.
executive_summary: Navier is the premium, zero-emission, software-defined edge of that renewal: fast corridors today's fleet can't serve, fully additive to your abra cooperative and aligned to your Marine Plan 2030 targets. Dubai 2040 sets a '20-minute city' goal and an expanding marine network; UAE Net Zero 2050 mandates decarbonization across every mode. Foiling is the premium edge of that renewal — faster and more efficient per passenger-mile, near-silent, zero-emission, and proven at network scale in the Maldives (2026). A demo vessel is in Dubai now.

narrative.headline: Phase 1 — Creek premium pilot
narrative.body: A small premium pilot on Dubai Creek and the Marina — proving the foiling tier in sheltered first-of-class waters, above the protected abra trade, with no new charging infrastructure beyond a home-berth pedestal.

narrative.headline: Phase 2 — Full inner-Dubai network
narrative.body: We light up the full inner network — Marina, Palm, Harbour, Creek and the Dubai Islands — as a premium decarbonized layer. Multi-rotation all-electric days, connecting the waterfront districts the road network struggles to serve.

narrative.headline: Phase 3 — Dubai ↔ Abu Dhabi express corridor
narrative.body: With the inner network proven, the long-range hybrid opens the corridor the region has always wanted: a fast, clean Dubai-to-Abu Dhabi water express — and the wider Gulf beyond — with no offshore charging dependency.

narrative.headline: Phase 4 — Southern Gulf foiling network
narrative.body: Steady state: 50+ foiling vessels run the full inner-Dubai mesh and a multi-daily Dubai↔Abu Dhabi express, with the Quanta-LR reach extending down the coast to Sir Bani Yas and the wider southern Gulf — the region's marine-transit fleet upgraded to foils, end to end.

partner_view.value_prop: We add a software-defined hydrofoiling tier to Dubai's marine transport network: quiet, zero-emission, and fast. It opens premium corridors the current fleet can't serve — a fast Creek premium service and a Dubai-to-Abu Dhabi express — and gives the authority a credible decarbonization path for water-bus and ferry renewal, all additive to existing services and fully aligned with Dubai 2040 and UAE Net Zero 2050.
partner_view.call_to_action: A Creek premium pilot, co-specified with RTA against the Marine Plan 2030 targets.

title: Navier × Fullers360 — the Hauraki Gulf, flying and clean
subtitle: Foiling-electric vessels for Auckland's zero-emission ferry future.
executive_summary: Navier delivers vessels that are zero-emission AND faster AND smoother across the Gulf chop — taking the high-frequency Waiheke and Devonport commuter legs, satisfying the decarbonization mandate, and opening longer Gulf island links the diesel fleet runs slowly today. Auckland Transport has committed to a low-emission ferry future and Fullers360 is decarbonizing its fleet. The Waiheke and Devonport commuter runs are busy and growing; the Gulf's longer island legs are slow on diesel. A tier that is clean AND faster is exactly what the mandate and the commuter need now.

narrative.headline: Phase 1 — Waiheke & Devonport commuter
narrative.body: Launch on the busy Waiheke and Devonport commuter runs — the highest-frequency, most visible Fullers360 corridors.

narrative.headline: Phase 2 — Hauraki Gulf islands
narrative.body: Scale across the Gulf — Rangitoto, Motutapu, Half Moon Bay and the outer islands — clean fast visitor and commuter links.

narrative.headline: Phase 3 — Northland & Coromandel corridor
narrative.body: Roughly 18 vessels forming a zero-emission foiling layer across the Hauraki Gulf, with Quanta-LR opening the premium coastal corridors to the Coromandel and the Bay of Islands.

partner_view.value_prop: Navier brings a software-defined foiling-electric fleet that meets Auckland's low-emission ferry mandate while flying faster and quieter than the diesel ferries it replaces. Fullers360 brings the wharves, the Hauraki Gulf network and the commuter demand — together modernizing one of the southern hemisphere's great ferry operations.
partner_view.call_to_action: Launch a Waiheke or Devonport pilot corridor in 2027 and scale across the Gulf as the diesel fleet retires.

title: Hawaiʻi × Navier — the Superferry, done right
subtitle: Quiet, low-wake, zero-emission foiling — the inter-island connection Hawaiʻi has been missing since 2009.
executive_summary: A foiling hull flies clear of the water — quiet, low-wake, zero-emission — the direct answer to every objection that grounded the Superferry. Navier reconnects your islands the way Hawaiʻi wished the Superferry had, and gives Pulama Lānaʻi a signature all-electric arrival experience. Hawaii has had no scheduled inter-island ferry since the Superferry shut down in 2009 — proven latent demand (300k+ passengers carried in under two years) with no clean way to serve it. Navier's software-defined foiling vessels lift clear of the water, eliminating the wake and whale-strike concerns that grounded the incumbent, and the Quanta-LR hybrid (commercial H2 2026+) needs no charging infrastructure at the outer harbors. Foiling is culturally native to the Pacific sailing world — the America's Cup connection makes 'is this proven?' an easy objection to answer.

narrative.headline: Phase 1 — Pulama Lānaʻi signature arrival
narrative.body: An all-electric foiling arrival to Four Seasons Lānaʻi across the sheltered ʻAuʻau Channel — the showcase that proves the platform in Hawaiian waters.

narrative.headline: Phase 2 — Maui County inter-island
narrative.body: Connect Maui, Lānaʻi, Molokaʻi and Hawaiʻi Island across channels no displacement craft can serve comfortably.

narrative.headline: Phase 3 — Statewide network with DOT Harbors
narrative.body: A clean, quiet statewide inter-island network anchored at Honolulu — restoring the connection Hawaiʻi lost in 2009.

partner_view.value_prop: We start with Pulama Lānaʻi: an all-electric foiling arrival to Four Seasons Lānaʻi across the sheltered ʻAuʻau Channel — a signature experience a private island owner can launch fast. Then we scale into the public inter-island network with Hawaiʻi DOT Harbors: Honolulu ↔ Molokaʻi, the ʻAlenuihāhā seasickness-relief crossing, and the Maui/Kauaʻi line-hauls — clean and quiet enough to clear the review that stopped the Superferry.
partner_view.call_to_action: A Pulama-Lānaʻi-anchored Phase 1 arrival to Four Seasons Lānaʻi, with a parallel DOT Harbors conversation on the inter-island network.

title: Navier × Hong Kong — the harbour and the crossing, re-platformed
subtitle: From the Star Ferry to the Macau run — foiling-electric across the world's busiest ferry waters.
executive_summary: Foiling-electric vessels modernize the fleet on every front at once: zero-emission for the harbour decarbonization mandate, faster and far smoother for the Macau/PRD crossings, and software-defined for an operating cost curve that keeps improving — the clean fleet-modernization narrative for the world's busiest ferry waters. Hong Kong has a stated harbour and ferry decarbonization mandate, with diesel ferry fleets facing replacement. The Macau and PRD sea crossings — among the busiest in the world — are under competitive pressure from the HZMB bridge and need a step-change to defend ridership. The Greater Bay Area integration agenda is pushing more cross-boundary passenger volume onto every available mode. Foiling-electric answers all three at once, exactly as the fleet-replacement cycle arrives.

narrative.headline: Phase 1 — Victoria Harbour modernization
narrative.body: Launch foiling-electric vessels on the Star Ferry and inner-harbour routes — the most visible, highest-frequency, decarbonization-mandated waters in the city.

narrative.headline: Phase 2 — outlying islands
narrative.body: Extend to Lamma, Cheung Chau, Mui Wo and Discovery Bay — the commuter and leisure outlying-island network — with faster, silent, frequent foiling links.

narrative.headline: Phase 3 — Macau & PRD crossings
narrative.body: Deploy Quanta-LR on the high-speed crossings to Macau and the Pearl River Delta — the competitive, high-value cross-boundary routes that defend the sea route against the bridge.

partner_view.value_prop: We modernize Hong Kong's passenger marine network with foiling-electric vessels — across Victoria Harbour, out to the outlying islands, and on the high-speed crossings to Macau and the Pearl River Delta. Navier supplies the software-defined fleet, captain training and certification path; the operator brings the routes, terminals, licences and the world's deepest ferry-passenger base. Together we turn an ageing diesel fleet into the cleanest, fastest, smoothest crossing in the region.
partner_view.call_to_action: A Victoria Harbour pilot MOU on two inner-harbour routes, with a defined path to the Macau crossing.

title: Navier × Indian Ocean — luxury island-hopping, reef-safe
subtitle: Re-platforming Seychelles, Mauritius and Zanzibar transfers on foiling-electric vessels.
executive_summary: Navier turns the transfer layer into a fast, smooth, all-weather, zero-emission, low-wake foiling network — protecting the reefs while transforming the guest experience, with the live Maldives network as the proof case next door. The Maldives network — ~100 vessels, $100M, phasing now — proved foiling-electric works at archipelago scale (WSJ + Bloomberg, May 2026). Seychelles, Mauritius and Zanzibar are the natural next clusters: same premium transfer demand, same reef-protection imperative, same weather-limited legacy fleet — and the proof case is already operating in the same ocean.

narrative.headline: Phase 1 — Seychelles inner islands
narrative.body: Launch on the Mahé–Praslin–La Digue inner-island transfers and resort hops — the densest, highest-value Seychelles corridors.

narrative.headline: Phase 2 — Mauritius lagoons
narrative.body: Scale to Mauritius — the east-coast lagoon resorts, Île aux Cerfs and the northern islets — fast coastal transfers replacing long road legs.

narrative.headline: Phase 3 — Zanzibar & the western network
narrative.body: Add Zanzibar — Stone Town to Nungwi and Mnemba, plus the all-weather Dar es Salaam mainland crossing — completing a western-Indian-Ocean foiling layer.

partner_view.value_prop: Navier brings a software-defined foiling-electric fleet that replaces rough diesel transfers and weather-bound air legs with fast, silent, low-wake island-hopping across the western Indian Ocean. The partnership pairs Navier's platform, captain training and certification path with regional resort relationships and island-by-island rollout — applying the live Maldives playbook to its sister archipelagos.
partner_view.call_to_action: Launch the Seychelles inner-island network in 2027 and extend the Maldives proof case across the western Indian Ocean.

title: Navier × Maldives — the flagship island-hopping network, live
subtitle: The transfer layer of the world's premier archipelago, re-platformed on foiling-electric vessels.
executive_summary: Navier already operates here. The Navier × JIH Global partnership is a live, at-scale deployment turning the transfer layer into a fast, smooth, all-weather, zero-emission foiling network — the proof case the rest of the world now points to. The Navier × JIH Global agreement — ~100 vessels, $100M, a three-year phased rollout with the first 5 boats in 2026 — was reported by The Wall Street Journal and Bloomberg in May 2026. It is the largest deployment of foiling-electric vessels in tourism, and it is already underway. The Maldives is no longer a pitch; it is the precedent.

narrative.headline: Phase 1 — Greater Malé & inner atolls
narrative.body: The first 5 vessels enter service on the highest-frequency airport-to-resort transfers across North and South Malé Atoll — the densest, most visible corridors in the country.

narrative.headline: Phase 2 — mid-atoll expansion
narrative.body: Scale across Ari, Baa and Lhaviyani atolls — the resort-dense mid-belt — adding Quanta-LR for the longer all-weather crossings that seaplanes can't fly after dark.

narrative.headline: Phase 3 — national network
narrative.body: Roughly 100 vessels at steady state forming a national foiling transfer layer spanning the inhabited atoll chain — the world's first archipelago-scale foiling network.

partner_view.value_prop: Through the Navier × JIH Global partnership we are deploying a foiling-electric vessel network across the Maldives — replacing rough diesel speedboat transfers and weather-bound seaplane legs with fast, silent, all-weather island-hopping. Navier brings the software-defined fleet, captain training and certification path; the partnership brings the resort relationships, the lagoon-by-lagoon rollout and the national footprint. This is the live case study every other archipelago is now measured against.
partner_view.call_to_action: Continue the phased deployment and publish the Maldives network as the global reference case for foiling island-hopping.

title: Navier × Fjord Norway — compliant, faster, silent
subtitle: Foiling-electric vessels for the world's strongest zero-emission marine mandate.
executive_summary: Navier delivers vessels that are not just zero-emission but faster, smoother and silent over the protected fjord water — satisfying the mandate while transforming the visitor and commuter experience across the world's most scenic, most regulated waterways. The 2026 zero-emission requirement in the UNESCO World Heritage fjords is the strongest pro-electric marine regulation anywhere. Norway has already built the supply chain, the charging norms and the public acceptance for electric vessels — what's missing is a tier that is clean and faster and silent. That is exactly Navier.

narrative.headline: Phase 1 — UNESCO fjord compliance (Geiranger)
narrative.body: The first vessels enter service on the Geirangerfjord/Nærøyfjord UNESCO legs where diesel sightseeing is now banned — the most acute, most visible mandate-driven demand.

narrative.headline: Phase 2 — Bergen fjord & commuter network
narrative.body: Scale across Bergen's fjord and commuter legs — Hardangerfjord, Osterfjord, island commuter runs — the dense gateway demand graph.

narrative.headline: Phase 3 — Stavanger & Lysefjord
narrative.body: Add the Stavanger/Ryfylke and Lysefjord network — Preikestolen sightseeing plus Ryfylke commuter demand.

narrative.headline: Phase 4 — national fjord & coastal-express network
narrative.body: Roughly 40+ vessels forming a national foiling fjord layer — the long Sognefjord and Bergen↔Stavanger coastal-express corridors on Quanta-LR, the fjord legs all-electric.

partner_view.value_prop: Navier brings a software-defined foiling-electric fleet that satisfies Norway's 2026 zero-emission fjord mandate while flying faster and quieter than the displacement ferries it replaces. The partnership pairs Navier's platform, captain training and certification path with the established Norwegian marine-electrification supply chain, charging norms and public acceptance — turning a regulatory forcing function into the best fjord experience on earth.
partner_view.call_to_action: Launch the mandate-critical UNESCO fjord legs in 2026 and publish Norway as the global zero-emission marine reference.

title: Saudi Arabia × Navier — the Kingdom's water-mobility platform
subtitle: PIF is building the coastline of Vision 2030. Navier is the foiling standard that connects it.
executive_summary: Navier can be your Saudi water-mobility platform across PIF's assets — one software-defined foiling standard from NEOM to the Red Sea to Jeddah to the Gulf coast — with a Turkey factory that makes regional and in-Kingdom localization credible. PIF's destinations are opening — The Red Sea is operating, AMAALA is coming online, NEOM is taking shape — and the mobility standard is being set right now. The opportunity is to own the premium, on-demand and long-range layer across all of PIF's coast — not one destination at a time.

narrative.headline: Phase 1 — The Red Sea + NEOM beachhead
narrative.body: Twelve vessels across PIF's flagship Red Sea coast: on-demand transfers in the Red Sea lagoon, the Red Sea↔AMAALA corridor, and NEOM's coastal nodes — the premium, long-range layer above the public shuttle.

narrative.headline: Phase 2 — Jeddah urban gateway
narrative.body: We light up Jeddah: corniche to Jeddah Central, on to KAEC and KAUST — the urban gateway that links the giga-project coast to a major city.

narrative.headline: Phase 3 — The national network + the Gulf coast
narrative.body: The Eastern Province ↔ Bahrain crossing relieves the most congested land border in the Gulf, while Quanta-LR through-runs stitch the Red Sea coast into one network — Navier as the Kingdom's water-mobility platform, with in-Kingdom localization.

partner_view.value_prop: We make Navier the water-mobility platform across PIF's destinations — NEOM, The Red Sea, AMAALA, Jeddah and the Eastern Province — one software-defined foiling fleet, one operating standard, with a path to in-Kingdom localization. Navier brings the platform and the network playbook proven in the Maldives; PIF brings the destinations, the demand and the Vision-2030 mandate.
partner_view.call_to_action: A platform framework with PIF: a Red Sea + NEOM pilot that sets the Kingdom-wide water-mobility standard.

narrative.headline: Phase 2 — Parramatta River network

narrative.headline: Phase 3 — Greater Sydney + coastal corridor
narrative.body: Roughly 20 vessels forming a zero-emission foiling layer across Greater Sydney's harbour and river network, with Quanta-LR opening the premium coastal corridor to Newcastle and the Central Coast.

partner_view.value_prop: Navier brings a software-defined foiling-electric fleet that satisfies NSW's zero-emission ferry mandate while flying faster and quieter than the diesel ferries it replaces. The partnership pairs Navier's platform, captain training and certification path with Transport for NSW's wharves, integrated-ticketing system and commuter demand — modernizing one of the world's great ferry networks.

title: Uber × Navier — the water layer of the world's mobility platform
subtitle: Uber aggregates demand and partners for supply. Navier is the foiling water supply — autonomy-ready, app-native, ready market by market.
executive_summary: Navier is the water-mobility supply layer for your demand engine: a software-defined, autonomy-ready foiling fleet that plugs into your app exactly like your robotaxi partners do — mode by mode, market by market. Pick one coastline or the whole network. Hydrofoiling lifts the hull clear of the water — roughly ten times more efficient than a conventional hull, faster, smoother, and quiet — and it needs no new infrastructure: it uses the oceans and berths that already exist, unlike flying taxis that need vertiports and fresh certification. The model is already real and ramping: a ~100-vessel network is being deployed in the Maldives ($100M, three-year phasing). Uber has shown it will put partner-operated autonomous fleets in its app; this is the same model on the water.

narrative.headline: Phase 1 — Proven clusters
narrative.body: Light up the markets that are already moving: the live Maldives network, the autonomous-forward Gulf, and the congested US coasts. One app integration, three demand graphs.

narrative.headline: Phase 2 — Coastal metros
narrative.body: Extend the same supply standard to the next tier of congested, water-rich metros — the Bay, the Mediterranean, and Sydney Harbour.

narrative.headline: Phase 3 — Every coastline
narrative.body: A uniform water tier in the Uber app wherever a coastline meets demand — the global water-mobility network.

partner_view.value_prop: Uber adds a foiling water tier the same way it adds robotaxis: Navier supplies the software-defined fleet and runs the network; Uber supplies the demand, the app, and the rider relationship. Below are the markets we can light up — choose where you want to move first.
partner_view.call_to_action: Pick a launch market — the Gulf, Miami, or the Bay are ready now — and scope a Phase-1 in-app foiling tier.
